companyIntro.name: Harbour Street Ventures
companyIntro.mission: Help small business owners and franchisees make money, not just stay busy.
companyIntro.culture: Know your numbers weekly. Cash is the scoreboard.

projectBackground.name: Franchise Evaluation Service — Quick Burger Franchise
projectBackground.context: A prospective franchisee is excited by the brand but hasn't checked the numbers. You advise on the deal.

manager.name: Maya Chen
manager.role: Head of Franchise Advisory, Harbour Street Ventures
manager.note: A franchise is a business you rent. Know what you pay, what you keep and how long it takes to get your money back.

assignment.title: Advise the prospective franchisee
assignment.brief: Calculate fees, payback and occupancy ratio, check due diligence and write a decision memo.

documents.name: Franchise Terms
documents.note: Initial fee 40,000; royalty 6% of sales; marketing fund 2%.

documents.name: Forecast
documents.note: Annual sales 500,000; operating profit after fees 45,000; rent 60,000.

documents.name: Franchisor Information
documents.note: Disclosure document lists 40% of units closed in three years.

tasks.title: Annual Fees
tasks.prompt: Annual sales 500,000; royalty 6% and marketing fund 2%. What are the annual ongoing fees?
tasks.reasoning: Ongoing fees come off the top line.
tasks.tip: Fees on sales, not on profit.
tasks.mistake: Forgetting the marketing fund understates cost.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Payback Period
tasks.prompt: Total investment 180,000; annual operating profit after fees 45,000. What is the payback (years)?
tasks.reasoning: Payback shows time to recover cash.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Occupancy Cost
tasks.prompt: Rent 60,000 on sales 500,000. What is occupancy cost (%)?
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Disclosure Document
tasks.prompt: Why is the franchise disclosure document important?
options: It gives the franchisor's fees, obligations, litigation and unit performance
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Due Diligence
options: Check territory rights and exit terms
Speak to current and former franchisees
tasks.tip: Ask former franchisees why they left.
tasks.mistake: Only talking to happy franchisees is biased.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Decision Memo
tasks.modelAnswer: The deal costs 180,000 and, after 40,000 in annual fees, returns 45,000 a year, a four-year payback with 12% occupancy cost. The disclosure shows 40% of units closed within three years, which is a serious warning. I recommend not signing until you speak to former franchisees, confirm territory protection and negotiate an exit clause. If closures are explained and exits are fair, the deal may be acceptable.
tasks.reasoning: A good memo weighs the numbers against the warning signs and sets conditions.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

caseStudy.title: Case Study: The Closed Units
caseStudy.background: A buyer ignored the disclosure's 38% closure rate. Two years later the unit closed and the family lost their savings.
caseStudy.solution: Harbour Street requires calls with three former franchisees before any advice.

prompts: Who would you call before signing?
What exit terms would you ask for?
